Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Light direction: side light — the light falls from one side, the far side of her face in soft shadow.
Outfit: a one-shoulder goddess gown of flowing chiffon gathered at one shoulder with a gold brooch, the other shoulder and arm bare, a thigh-high slit — in clean neutrals such as white, ivory, oatmeal or soft grey; the outfit colour reads clearly at first glance; fabric weight — its knit or thin-fabric pieces (a top, an inner top or a knit dress) are 80-denier yarn, semi-sheer so her skin tone and body line show softly through, with a fully opaque lining over the bust and the hips; any tights or stockings are sheer 60-denier nylon; shorts, skirts, leather, denim and other heavy materials stay opaque, showing her shoulders, collarbones and legs as far as the outfit allows, following her curvy figure — a slim waist and rounded hips; intimate areas covered.

COMPOSITION: a close-up of her face and hair; body facing the camera; head tilted slightly; camera slightly below, looking up at her.
Lens / perspective: 85mm-equivalent short-telephoto perspective from a suitable distance, with gentle background compression.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand makes a V sign beside her face.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand stays outside the frame.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: softly lowered brows, warm relaxed eyes, faint closed-lip smile, no tension anywhere.

Framing: a close-up — her face and hair fill most of the frame and the bottom edge crosses at her collarbones; nothing below the shoulders shows, and her hands and anything she holds stay below the frame unless raised to her face.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — iodine: born in 1811 when Bernard Courtois, a Paris saltpetre maker, saw a violet vapor rise from seaweed ash, and named for the Greek word for violet; lustrous blue-black crystals that skip the liquid and sublime straight into violet vapor, then frost back into crystals on anything cold; the amber-brown tincture painted on wounds, the pinch in iodized salt that keeps the thyroid well; turns starch a deep blue-black; its vapor sensitized the silver plates of the first daguerreotypes; the gentlest and heaviest stable halogen, a healer of the sea who vanishes into mist and reappears — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, logo or watermark.
